extracted.intended_audience: pun contest contestants, punsters, judges, and event attendees
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and judging criteria for the O. Henry Museum Pun-Off World Championships, covering two competitions (Punniest of Show and Punslingers), time limits, scoring, elimination mechanics, and acceptable topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a pun
rubrics_metrics.description: A pun is the humorous use of a word or words in such a way as to suggest different meanings or applications OR words that have the same or nearly the same sound but different meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes homophones as a common form: "Just think homophones and you’re most of the way there." It also notes subjective judgments: "even WE sometimes disagree on what is actually a pun. And we’re good at this!" — implying judges have discretion in what qualifies as a pun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punniest of Show — prepared performance, time limits, disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepared "punny" material delivered within specified time limits: a maximum of 32 contestants, allowed 90 seconds before a "soft" bell, may continue after soft bell but at 2 minutes a "hard" bell is sounded and the contestant will be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are prepared material (as opposed to spontaneous rounds). Time enforcement: soft bell at 90 seconds (warning), hard bell at 2 minutes (disqualification). Judges rank entries on a 1-10 scale; a cumulative score is recorded; the three top scoring contestants are recognized as winners. In case of a tie score, the audience will be asked to help decide a championship round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punslingers — head-to-head rapid punning, turns, strikes, elimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapid, head-to-head punning: up to 32 contestants paired for head-to-head rounds; each pair is given a topic; at the judge’s signal players alternate turns with 5 seconds to deliver or begin a pun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn mechanics: each player has 5 seconds to deliver or begin delivering a pun; the opponent then has 5 seconds, and this continues. A contestant loses a round if they cannot make a pun (become "tongue-tied") or accumulate a total of three non-qualifying "strike" attempts at a pun. Eliminations proceed in standard tournament style until a final winner. If an odd number of surviving punsters occurs in later rounds, a three-way contest may be used (eliminating one contestant) and the quick-draw format continues on the same topic until a winner is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring, advancement, and tie-breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: How winners are determined differs by event: Punniest of Show uses judge scoring and cumulative totals; Punslingers uses head-to-head elimination based on failures/strikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punniest of Show: entries are "ranked on a 1-10 scale by our judges panel" and cumulative scores determine top three winners. Tie procedure: audience decides a championship round. Punslingers: advancement is by eliminating contestants who fail to produce qualifying puns (three strikes) or cannot continue; no numeric score is described for Punslingers—progression is tournament/elimination-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional topics and topic-specific restrictions for Punslingers
rubrics_metrics.description: A long list of common/traditional topics used in Punslingers, some with explicit restrictions noted in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Topics enumerated on the page: Competition; Religion; Biology & Chemistry; Colors/Art & Artists; Radio & Television; Carpentry/Construction; Flowers; Education; Money & Finance; Wheeled Vehicles; Medicine (no body parts); Winged Creatures; Wild Animals; Movies & Theater; Food & Cooking; Male Names; Clothing; Computers/Electronics; American Cities; Airborne Vehicles; Books & Authors; Oil Business; Trees; Astronomy & Astrology; Archeology; Female Names; Sea Creatures; Farming & Ranching; Insects & Bugs; Drinks; Politics; Diseases; Internal Body Parts; Popular Music; The Law & Crime; Rock & Roll Music; Jazz & Classical Music; Physical Sports; Child’s Play (toys & games); Weather; Shrinks & Psychology; Military; Holidays; Indians & Aboriginals; External Body Parts; Country Music; Fruits & Vegetables; Bodies of Water (specific or general); Europe, Asia, & Australia (countries only); Countries of the World (no cities or states); Ceramics and Glass and Related Terms; Mathematics & Physics; Furniture & Furnishings; Waterborne Vehicles; Nuclear Energy; Dogs; Cats; Domestic animals (other than cats & dogs); Gambling.

Note the parenthetical constraints explicitly called out: "Medicine (no body parts)" and "Countries of the World (no cities or states)" and the restriction on "Domestic animals (other than cats & dogs)." These indicate topical restrictions that competitors must observe when puns are assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' signal, discretion, and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges control the start of turns in Punslingers and evaluate entries in Punniest of Show; they have discretion about what counts as a qualifying pun or strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states "At the judge’s signal, each player...will have 5 seconds to deliver..." and judges rank Punniest entries on a 1-10 scale. Combined with the earlier note about subjective disagreement over what is a pun, this implies judges both enforce timing/turn order and exercise judgment in calling non-qualifying attempts (strikes) or scoring performances.
